profile.reading: This is Bloombergs data center at 155 Corporate Drive in Orangeburg, in the Town of Orangetown, Rockland County, New York, about 25 miles north of New York City. The 143,331 square foot building was formerly owned by Verizon before being acquired by Russo Development Corporation in 2009, and Bloomberg does not own the building outright, per industry directory Baxtel. Bloomberg announced the project in May 2013 as a planned 710 million dollar investment over 15 years, including about 435 million dollars for initial renovation and equipment, after evaluating roughly 100 candidate sites across New York and New Jersey. Utility documents reviewed in coverage of the project describe up to 40 megawatts of provisioned electrical capacity available at the site through four 13 kilovolt circuits of 10 megawatts each, fed by subterranean 138 kilovolt ring bus transmission lines, though this figure represents capacity made available to the site rather than a confirmed fully built out IT load. The facility supports Bloomberg L.P.s trading and financial data infrastructure, with proximity to New York financial market connectivity hubs cited as a key site selection factor; Bloomberg is reported to operate at least two other data centers in the broader New York and New Jersey region as part of its East Coast infrastructure. Bloomberg L.P. is a privately held financial data, media, and software company founded in 1981 by Michael Bloomberg, who retains roughly 88 percent ownership, reporting about 15 billion dollars in revenue in 2024. Orangetown and the surrounding Rockland County area have attracted other large corporate back office and technology facilities over the years due to their position within reasonable commuting and network latency distance of Manhattan while offering lower real estate costs, a pattern common among financial sector technology infrastructure sited in the broader New York metropolitan region.

reading.body:
Bloomberg's Orangeburg data center sits on 143,000 square feet in Rockland County, about 25 miles north of New York City, in a building formerly owned by Verizon. The operator announced in May 2013 a planned 710 million dollar investment over 15 years, with an initial 435 million dollars budgeted for renovation and equipment. Utility documents describe up to 40 megawatts of provisioned electrical capacity available through four 10 megawatt circuits fed by 138 kilovolt transmission lines, though this represents capacity made available to the site rather than confirmed built-out IT load; at 25 kilowatts per rack, a conservative density for financial data workloads, 40 megawatts of IT load would be roughly 1,600 racks, though actual occupancy is not published.

The facility is designed to support Bloomberg L.P.'s trading and financial data infrastructure, with site selection driven by proximity to New York financial market connectivity hubs and lower real estate costs than Manhattan while maintaining reasonable network latency. Bloomberg does not own the building outright and operates at least two other data centers in the broader New York and New Jersey region as part of its East Coast infrastructure. Completion status after the May 2013 announcement has not been independently verified; a tracker showed a permit application marked proposed as of January 2024.

In New York state, 31 data center facilities are mapped, but only one facility has published megawatt specifications to this site: this one, at 40 megawatts, ranks second in the state by published capacity and accounts for the state's entire published 3 megawatt total. This rank reflects the opacity of the state's data center inventory rather than dominance of the campus itself.
